title: Superflow vs Marker.io
kicker: · SUPERFLOW VS MARKER.IO · THE AI QA REVIEWER FOR AGENCIES
headline: Marker.io is a bug reporting tool. Superflow is a bug reporting tool + a team.
secondary: The team is AI agents, built from your QA checklist. They check every site change and pin what they find. Your team decides. Your client approves from a link.
prevents: Stop finding every mistake by hand.
No more manual pass before launch.
qualifier: If your agency reviews client sites in Marker.io, this page is for you.
heroCaption: It's like Marker.io hired a QA team.

dimensions.label: Who checks the site
dimensions.framing: Marker.io was built before AI could check a site.
leftFacts: Agents run your checklist. Every change, desktop and mobile.
Findings land as pinned comments, rationale attached.
rightFacts: A person finds every issue, then reports it.
Its AI edits, translates, and titles report text.
Its MCP sends bug context to outside AI agents like Claude and Cursor, useful for dev handoff. Nothing in Marker.io looks at the site to find problems.
dimensions.verdict: A bug report is a record of what a person already caught. That's the part Superflow removes.

dimensions.label: How the client says yes
dimensions.framing: Feedback is easy to collect. A yes is harder.
leftFacts: Multi-step review flows: agents check, your team gates, then the client.
Your client opens a link and taps Approve. No account, no login, no app, from their phone.
rightFacts: Reporters submit free from the widget, no account, and can follow their own issues.
Ongoing client collaborators are paid guest seats: 10 on Starter, 50 on Team.
A formal approval flow: not yet verified.
dimensions.verdict: Marker.io's free reporting is good. The difference is the gate: in Superflow, the client's yes is a recorded step, not a comment.

dimensions.label: Where you review
dimensions.framing: Half of client work lives behind a password.
leftFacts: Superflow lives on the site itself: passwords, Okta, SSO, no extension needed, guests included.
rightFacts: You annotate a screenshot capture of the page; the report carries the picture, not a persistent on-page pin.
Widget on the live site, browser extension for members on any webpage.
dimensions.verdict: Superflow reviews the page itself, live, behind logins and SSO. Marker.io files a picture of it. Behind logins, the Marker.io side is pending verification.

dimensions.label: What stays private
dimensions.framing: Your team needs somewhere to disagree.
leftFacts: Internal-only notes your team sees and the client never does.
The debate stays private; the client sees one settled answer.
rightFacts: Internal comments on every plan, including Starter.
dimensions.verdict: Close to even. Marker.io ships internal comments on every plan, including its entry tier, the same job Superflow's internal-only comments do.

dimensions.label: What gets captured
dimensions.framing: Both tools pin. The difference is what gets attached without asking.
leftFacts: Element and text pins, area comments.
A screenshot attaches to every comment automatically.
Recordings: screen, video, voice, from the toolbar.
rightFacts: Screenshot capture plus environment details (browser, OS, webpage, screen size) on every plan.
Console logs, network requests, and session replay of the last three minutes, on the Team plan and up.
dimensions.verdict: Marker.io's technical capture is genuinely strong. It just starts on the Team plan. Superflow's screenshots and recordings ship on every plan.

dimensions.label: What it remembers
dimensions.framing: Boards hold tasks. They don't accumulate a client.
leftFacts: Brand rules and past decisions, learned once, fed to the agents next project.
rightFacts: No memory concept. Each project starts blank.
dimensions.verdict: The tenth project should not start like the first.

dimensions.label: How it fits your stack
dimensions.framing: The fix still has to ship.
leftFacts: Two-way Asana, Monday, ClickUp. Slack built in.
rightFacts: Feedback becomes a ticket in your tracker; the tracker is the workspace.
Thirteen-plus integrations, dev-side especially: GitHub, GitLab, Linear, Bitbucket. Jira from the Team plan. Azure DevOps plan gate: not yet verified.
Two-way Issue sync is real, but a Team plan feature: Done in Jira flips to Resolved in Marker.io.
dimensions.verdict: If your delivery runs on a dev tracker, Marker.io fits it deeply. We sync two-way with Asana, Monday, and ClickUp. We have no built-in Jira sync today.

pricingCompetitor: Verified July 2026: Starter $39/mo annual ($59 monthly), 3 users, 10 projects, 10 guests, 5k page views/mo. Team $149/mo annual ($199 monthly), 15 users, 50 projects, 50 guests, 25k page views/mo. Business custom, yearly only. No free plan. 15-day trial, no card.
switchingLines: One snippet on any site; one click on Webflow, WordPress, or GTM.
Paste the checklist you already have; agents assemble from it.
Open Marker.io projects finish in Marker.io. Nothing migrates on day one.
honestCloseStrengths: Marker.io earned its place. Feedback becomes a ticket in the tracker your team already runs, and status syncs back on the Team plan. Console logs, network requests, and session replay attach to reports with real technical depth, on the Team plan and up. Reporters are free and unlimited, no account needed.
stayLine: If a careful human pass filed into the tracker you already run works for your team, and your developers want console logs, network requests, and session replay attached to every report, Marker.io is a strong fit. Stay.

faq.question: Is Superflow just Marker.io with AI on top?
faq.answer: No. Marker.io's AI edits and retitles what a person already reported; Superflow's agents do the finding. A person makes every call.

faq.question: Do the agents replace my reviewers?
faq.answer: No. Agents run the first pass. Your team, then your client, signs off.

faq.question: What happens to our Marker.io projects?
faq.answer: Finish them in Marker.io. Start new work in Superflow. Nothing migrates on day one.

faq.question: Will our clients have to learn a new tool?
faq.answer: No. They get a link and an Approve button. No account, no login, no app, from their phone.

faq.question: We push tickets to Jira from Marker.io.
faq.answer: Superflow syncs two-way with Asana, Monday, and ClickUp, plus webhooks and a REST API. Jira is not built in today; if Jira runs your delivery, weigh that.
